verdict.rationale: Supermemory's security docs describe per-user erasure: scope each end-user to a container tag, then delete that container's content via the API or console. Document operations separately support deleting individual ingested documents. However, deleting a single extracted memory (as distinct from a document) and full account- or org-wide erasure are not explicitly documented. Missing for 10: explicit single-memory delete endpoint, documented full-erasure/account-wide purge, confirmation that derived graph/profile facts are purged, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can delete a user's memories on demand — single memory, per-entity, or full erasure — to satisfy privacy requirements
